key_insight: An additive thermodynamic correction layer aligns machine learning interatomic potentials with assessed phase thermodynamics without retraining the base model.
engineering_relevance: The approach enables more accurate melting and solid–solid transformation predictions while retaining transferable atomistic models.
method: Convert required phase free-energy shifts into configuration energy targets using a first-order thermodynamic construction.
Fit an additive linear atomic cluster expansion correction.
Refine the correction iteratively using measured free energies.
evidence_signal: Tests with a foundation GRACE model brought all evaluated transformation temperatures within prescribed tolerances, including simultaneous solid–solid and melting corrections for Ca, Ti, and Zr.
watch_item: Large corrections can alter vacancy formation energies, thermal expansion, and liquid density, so these properties require validation.
paper_title: A thermodynamic correction layer for machine learning interatomic potentials
